candidates.reason: It is a real rearrangement and the headline is large and readable. But the oversized Quillbrook roundel competes with the headline for attention. The 'Free delivery' subcopy is cut off from the headline and squeezed into a small 3-line stack beside the button, close to the right edge. The bottom of the button nearly touches the canvas edge, and the headline wraps with 'Monday' left on its own line.

Nearly the same as candidate 1, but the roundel is a little bigger, which makes it compete with the headline even more. The subcopy sits even closer to the right edge, and the button is pushed lower toward the bottom edge. It has the same split of the headline from its supporting copy and the same orphaned 'Monday'.

This is the original strip scaled down and stretched out rather than rearranged. The headline and the 'Free delivery' line are pulled apart by a large unexplained gap, so they no longer read as one block. The logo is tiny and its QUILLBROOK wordmark can't be read. The Shop Coffee button is jammed against the right edge, and the top and bottom of the canvas are dead space.

This is a shrunk copy of the original banner: one thin band in the middle with large empty bands above and below, so it doesn't suit the taller format. The logo is tiny and its wordmark can't be read, the subcopy is small, and the Shop Coffee button nearly touches the right edge. The internal grouping is still correct, which puts it ahead of candidate 3.
